ayuntamiento: In Spain and Spanish America, a corporation or body of magistrates in cities and towns, corresponding to mayor and aldermen.
aye: Yes; yea; -- a word expressing assent, or an affirmative answer to a question. It is much used in viva voce voting in legislative bodies, etc. Note: This word is written I in the early editions of… | An affirmative vote; one who votes in the affirmative; as, "To call for the ayes and noes;" "The ayes have it."
ayah: A native nurse for children; also, a lady's maid. [India]
ayme: The utterance of the ejaculation "Ay me !" (old) See Ay, interj. "Aymees and hearty heigh-hoes." J. Fletcher.
ayle: A grandfather. (old) Writ of Ayle, an ancient English writ which lay against a stranger who had dispossessed the demandant of land of which his grandfather died seized.
ayrshire: One of a superior breed of cattle from Ayrshire, Scotland. Ayrshires are notable for the quantity and quality of their milk.
ayeaye: A singular nocturnal quadruped, allied to the lemurs, found in Madagascar (Cheiromys Madagascariensis), remarkable for its long fingers, sharp nails, and rodent-like incisor teeth.
